title: Army gives 25 sewing machines to women at Kanto Sabal
summary: The handover in Imphal West under Operation Sadbhavana is meant to help women earn through tailoring.
body:
The Indian Army has handed 25 sewing machines to women at Kanto Sabal in Imphal West district, under its Operation Sadbhavana outreach programme.

An Army official said the aim is to help the women learn tailoring, start small businesses and add to their household income.

The Army's earlier community work in the area included solar street lights, water supply and furniture for local residents and schools.

Operation Sadbhavana, which means goodwill, was started by the Army's Northern Command in Jammu and Kashmir in 1998. It began as a civic action programme for people living in areas hit by militancy, and it was later carried out in Ladakh and the Northeastern states as well. Its stated focus includes education, women's empowerment, health care and community infrastructure.

The idea behind such work is older than the programme itself. Army units posted in the Northeast during the early years of insurgency held medical camps and supplied basic goods in remote villages, small efforts that later grew into larger civic programmes.

This is not the first time women at Kanto Sabal have received sewing machines from the Army. In March 2025, the Army gave six machines to women in the village under a similar initiative, and women from Khurkul village also took part in that event, according to a release by the defence public relations office.

The Army said the new machines should help the women build practical skills and set up small tailoring units, many of which can be run from home. It described the handover as part of its wider community work across Manipur, which it says is meant to meet local needs, encourage self-reliance and build trust between soldiers and residents. Local women who received the machines thanked the Army and said the support would help them earn on their own.
